name: Humbug
description: Humbug is a minimalist 18th-century trick-taking game for two players, representing the simplest possible adaptation of Whist. It is unique because both players are dealt the entire deck, making it a game of perfect information (after the initial overview) and a rigorous test of memory and card counting.

content.text: Humbug is a minimalist 18th-century trick-taking game for two players, representing the simplest possible adaptation of Whist. It is unique because both players are dealt the entire deck, making it a game of perfect information (after the initial overview) and a rigorous test of memory and card counting.
Documented in London publications as early as 1793 (e.g., The Sporting Magazine). It was designed as a high-stakes gambling game for two people who wanted the rigor of Whist without needing partners.

Exactly two players. Humbug was designed as a high-stakes two-hand whist variant for two people who wanted the rigor of Whist without partners; it is documented in London publications from the 1790s (e.g. The Sporting Magazine).

Deal all 52 cards, one at a time. The final card (belonging to the dealer) is turned up to determine the Trump suit. Both players then layout their hand face-up by suit to see the complete game state.
